signature.name: Victoria Peak
signature.detail: The highest point on Hong Kong Island offers sweeping views of the skyline and Victoria Harbour, making it the city's most iconic sight. Take the historic Peak Tram from Central; go early morning or late evening to avoid crowds and catch the best light.

signature.name: Victoria Harbour
signature.detail: This legendary harbor separates Hong Kong Island and Kowloon, with dramatic views of skyscrapers and the nightly Symphony of Lights show. Best experienced from the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront or via the Star Ferry; arrive before 8pm for the light show.

signature.name: Tian Tan Buddha
signature.detail: The giant bronze Buddha on Lantau Island is a must-see, reached by the scenic Ngong Ping 360 cable car or bus. Climb the 268 steps for panoramic views; go on a clear day and avoid weekends for fewer crowds.

signature.name: Avenue of Stars
signature.detail: This waterfront promenade in Tsim Sha Tsui honors Hong Kong's film stars and offers stunning views of the harbor and skyline. Visit at dusk to see the lights come on; it's free and easily accessible via the East Tsim Sha Tsui MTR.

signature.name: Star Ferry
signature.detail: A historic ferry crossing Victoria Harbour between Tsim Sha Tsui and Central, offering a cheap and scenic ride. Ride at sunset for magical views; use your Octopus card for a hassle-free trip.

signature.name: Man Mo Temple
signature.detail: One of Hong Kong's oldest temples, dedicated to the gods of literature and war, with impressive incense coils hanging from the ceiling. It's free to enter; dress respectfully and visit early to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
signature.detail: A bustling Taoist temple known for granting wishes, with colorful architecture and fortune-tellers. Take the MTR to Wong Tai Sin station; go in the morning to see locals praying.

signature.name: Bank of China Tower
signature.detail: An iconic skyscraper designed by I.M. Pei, with a distinctive triangular facade. While the observation deck is closed, admire it from Victoria Harbour or the Peak; it's especially striking at night.

signature.name: Mid-Levels Escalators
signature.detail: The world's longest outdoor covered escalator system, running through the Mid-Levels and SoHo. Ride it uphill after 10am (it runs downhill in the morning); hop off to explore the shops and restaurants along the way.

signature.name: Ngong Ping 360
signature.detail: A spectacular cable car ride to Ngong Ping Village and the Tian Tan Buddha, with views over Lantau Island and the sea. Book tickets online to skip queues; opt for a crystal cabin for glass-bottom views.

transport: Metro $1-2 a ride; taxis moderate; Octopus card recommended
